title: Tortilla Chips 300g

drivers.name: Price increase to $3.97
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $3.97 saw 106 and 75 units (vs baseline 124.2), median x0.70. Noise-adjusted estimate for price effect: x0.80.

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: One day closure in a 7-day week reduces expected sales by ~14%. No prior closure data, but store-level closure effects are typically linear.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 124.2. The target week has a price increase to $3.97 (+3.7% vs regular $3.83) and a store closure on Monday. Price increases reduce demand; historical data shows a 3.97 price week (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) averaged 106 and 75 units (vs baseline 124.2), implying a ~20% demand drop. The store closure on Monday (1/7 of the week) likely reduces sales by ~14% of the week’s volume. No promotion or event is planned. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but judgment overrides this: price and closure are clear, named drivers. Combine multiplicative: 0.80 (price) × 0.86 (closure) = 0.69. Shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence (one price spike, one closure), yielding median_multiplier 0.75. Spreads widen slightly due to uncertainty in closure impact and price sensitivity. Confidence is medium.

brief:
PRODUCT: Tortilla Chips 300g | category Snacks | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 3.97 (+3.7% vs regular price 3.83)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 124.2 | 5%-95%: 77.5 - 200.4 | 10%-90%: 88.9 - 170.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-29% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
